cards.text: Nehemiah tells this one himself. He serves King Artaxerxes, and the king has let him travel home to Jerusalem, the city where his fathers are buried (Nehemiah 2:1-6). Three days pass after he arrives, which is ADORABLE to a stamper who spent YEARS in a junk drawer.

cards.question: Nehemiah finally heads out to look around Jerusalem with just a few men. When does he go?
God has laid something on Nehemiah's heart to do for Jerusalem. Who has Nehemiah told about it?

cards.text: Just a few men and one animal, the one he's riding. Quietest parade in history. Out through the Valley Gate he goes, toward the Well of the Serpent and the Dung Gate.

cards.question: Riding out in the dark, Nehemiah inspects the broken ___ and the burned ___ of Jerusalem.

cards.text: Next stop, the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool. And right here, friend, the night tour hits a snag.

cards.question: What's the snag for Nehemiah at the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool?

answers.text: No room for his animal to pass
A guard won't let him through
The pool has flooded the path

cards.question: Since his animal can't get through, Nehemiah calls it a night and skips the rest of the wall.
Nehemiah goes up the valley by night to inspect the wall, then heads back in through the ___ Gate, the same one he left by.

cards.text: Back in town, the officials have no clue where he went or what he was doing. Then Nehemiah speaks up: “You see the trouble we are in. Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned down.”

cards.question: Jerusalem is in ruins and its gates are burned. What does Nehemiah say they should do about it?

answers.text: Ask the king to send builders

cards.question: Nehemiah says that rebuilding the wall means they will no longer be a disgrace.

cards.text: Then he tells them about the gracious hand of his God on him, and what the king said to him. No slideshow. No handouts. Just a man, his God and the king's word.

cards.question: After hearing about God's gracious hand and the king's words, the people tell Nehemiah they need time to think it over.

cards.text: The people set their hands to this good work. Then word reaches Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official and Geshem the Arab, and friend, uh-oh.

cards.question: What do Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem do when they hear about the rebuilding?

answers.text: Offer to help with the wall

cards.question: Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem ask the builders if they are ___ against the king.
Nehemiah answers the mockers. Who does he say will grant the builders success?
Nehemiah tells Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem that they have a claim in Jerusalem too.

cards.text: Then the rebuilding starts, crew next to crew all the way around: Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests at the Sheep Gate, goldsmiths, perfumers, and Shallum, a district ruler, with the help of his daughters, until the last stretch meets the Sheep Gate again. The Tekoite nobles don't put their shoulders to the work, but the wall is coming back, and friend, this story's not done.

findings.problem: Story card has three sentences: "Just a few men and one animal, the one he's riding." / "Quietest parade in history." / "Out through the Valley Gate he goes...". Only the opening card may go up to 3.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 4 already told the baker Nehemiah went out through the Valley Gate, and the question adds "the same one he left by." Together they give the answer away, so the card tests nothing.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Story card has four sentences: the retelling, "No slideshow.", "No handouts." and "Just a man, his God and the king's word."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup ends with "and friend, uh-oh," which signals trouble before card 16 asks how Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem react. That rules out the wrong answer "Offer to help with the wall."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Shallum is called "a district ruler." The text calls him "ruler of the other half-district of Jerusalem" (Neh 3:12).

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The story-continues line "and friend, this story's not done" copies the doc's example ("Trust me, friend, this story's not done.") almost word for word instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
